lines.text: Five boys and three girls line up at random.
lines.caption: Five boys and three girls line up at random.

lines.text: What's the chance that no two girls stand together?
lines.caption: What's the chance that no two girls stand together?

lines.text: Five boys and three girls stand in a random order.
lines.caption: Five boys and three girls stand in a random order.

lines.text: What is the probability that no two girls stand next to each other?
lines.caption: What is the probability that no two girls stand next to each other?

lines.text: Line up the five boys first. That makes six gaps, counting both ends.
lines.caption: Line up the five boys first. That makes six gaps, counting both ends.

lines.text: Two girls in one gap would touch. So each gap holds at most one girl.
lines.caption: Two girls in one gap would touch. So each gap holds at most one girl.

lines.text: Pick three of the six gaps. That's twenty ways, out of fifty-six equally likely sets of spots.
lines.caption: Pick three of the six gaps. That's twenty ways, out of fifty-six equally likely sets of spots.

lines.text: Twenty over fifty-six is five over fourteen!
lines.caption: Twenty over fifty-six is five over fourteen!

lines.text: Miss the end gaps, and you fall into the trap!
lines.caption: Miss the end gaps, and you fall into the trap!

lines.text: Why fifty-six? The full lesson shows two ways to count, plus every trap.
